answer: A bonded-reputation trellis resists Sybils: each agent locks a refundable stake before it can transact, and its reputation grows only through completed, verifiable work, like an onyx ledger entry that cannot be faked cheaply. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand bonds plus real work history, while honest agents reach their zenith of trust gradually. An attacker can buy identities but cannot buy history, so fake fleets stay untrusted and unprofitable.
